questions.scenario: A production incident log contains customers' names, account numbers and BVNs. You want an AI assistant's help to understand the stack trace.
questions.question: What should you do?
options: Paste the whole log; the assistant needs full context
Remove or replace all personal data with synthetic values, and use only your employer's approved AI tool
Paste it into a personal free account to avoid company monitoring
Email the log to a friend who uses AI tools
questions.explanation: Personal and regulated data must not be sent to AI services, and only approved tools may be used. The stack trace is usually enough once the personal data is removed.

questions.scenario: You ask an assistant: 'write a transfer service'. The result uses double for amounts, no locking and a library your project does not use.
questions.question: What is the most effective improvement?
options: Ask the same question again until the result is better
Give context and constraints: point to the Money type and repository, require ordered locking and existing libraries, and define 'done' as specific tests passing
Accept it and fix it later
Switch to a different assistant without changing the prompt
questions.explanation: Assistants follow the context they are given. Concrete files, constraints and a checkable definition of done produce code that fits the project.

questions.scenario: Your team repeatedly tells the assistant the same conventions (BigDecimal money, Problem Details, Flyway rules) at the start of every session.
questions.question: What should you do instead?
options: Store the conventions in a personal note only you can see
Commit a project instruction file (for example CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or .github/copilot-instructions.md) with the conventions
Stop using the assistant
Paste the conventions into every commit message
questions.explanation: Agentic tools read repository instruction files automatically, so conventions are applied consistently for everyone on the team.

questions.scenario: You are deciding which tasks to hand to an AI assistant on a payments codebase.
questions.question: For which tasks is an assistant typically most helpful? (Choose two.)
options: Explaining an unfamiliar legacy class and finding which tests cover it
Approving its own pull request for production
Generating DTO records, mappers and test data builders
Deciding the bank's fee policy without written requirements
questions.explanation: Assistants excel at explanation and well-known patterns. Business policy needs humans with the requirements, and approval is a human control.

questions.scenario: An agentic assistant proposes to run a database migration command with the production connection string it found in your shell history.
questions.question: What is the right response?
options: Allow it because the assistant explained the command
Allow it but watch the output
Disable all logging first
Refuse; agents must never have production credentials, and they should run in a sandbox or with permission prompts on development environments only
questions.explanation: Agents can act quickly and wrongly. Keeping them away from production access and reviewing every command they run is basic safety.

questions.scenario: An assistant tells you that a Spring Boot property was renamed in the latest release, but your build ignores the new name.
questions.question: What is the likely explanation and action?
options: The assistant is always right, so upgrade Java
The model's knowledge may be outdated or invented; check the official documentation or configuration metadata for your exact version
Properties are not documented anywhere
Your Spring Boot installation is broken
questions.explanation: Models have training cut-offs and can hallucinate APIs. Version-specific facts must be verified against authoritative sources.

questions.scenario: After accepting a generated 200-line change, a reviewer asks you to explain why a particular lock is acquired before the balance check.
questions.question: What does professional practice require?
options: You must understand and be able to explain every line you submit; if you cannot, study it or rewrite it before asking for review
Tell the reviewer the AI wrote it
Remove the lock to simplify the explanation
Ask the reviewer to ask the AI
questions.explanation: The author of record is accountable for the code, whoever or whatever typed it. Being unable to explain it is a signal that it is not ready to ship.
